assumptions: All node availability probabilities and common-cause event probabilities are synthetic sensitivity inputs and are not operator or vendor reliability claims.
The three HAPS nodes have independent baseline availability 0.98, conditional on no shared HAPS weather grounding event.
The terrestrial gateway and LEO backhaul nodes have independent baseline availability values 0.995 and 0.99, conditional on no shared external common-mode event.
The weather event disables all three HAPS nodes together; the shared external event disables terrestrial and LEO fallback together. The two common-cause events are independent in this case.
The service is available if at least one of the five provider nodes remains operational after its independent and common-cause states are applied.
No shared dependencies are required in this case; the two common-cause events explicitly represent the shared dependencies between provider groups.
The naïve k-of-n comparator treats all five provider nodes as independent and ignores both common-cause events; the exact enumeration includes them.

This is a static Bernoulli probability model over a 30-day declared analysis window; it does not model outage duration, weather episode persistence, repair, maintenance scheduling, geographic overlap, capacity or handover.
The 99.99% target is an illustrative synthetic objective, not an operator SLA or achieved service availability.

A third synthetic cross-layer common-cause event with probability 0.005 affects all five provider nodes at once, representing a severe regional hazard / common ground-control dependency stress case. Its per-window probability is invented for sensitivity testing, not empirically estimated.
The third event is a single Bernoulli variable affecting HAPS, terrestrial and LEO providers together; it is not modeled as three or five independent failures.

Five independent provider availability bits and three independent common-cause event bits produce 2^8 = 256 exact states. The exact fleet availability is the prior two-common-cause result multiplied by (1 - 0.005) because the new event disables all provider nodes whenever it occurs.
The naïve comparator continues to ignore all three common-cause events, intentionally exposing the false independence assumption.
